task_instruction: Write a close third-person scene from Ilya’s perspective as she tries to bind a fleeing oathbreaker in a courthouse archive using the true-name binding ritual.
source_state: Ilya (she/her) is a licensed oath-scribe in a courthouse archive. She must stop a fleeing oathbreaker named Corven Hale before he reaches the outer records door. The binding ritual has strict rules: it only works if Ilya speaks the target’s true name; it can prevent movement for sixty heartbeats but cannot force speech, confession, truth, pain, sleep, or obedience; the caster pays by losing one accurate personal memory chosen by the spell at the moment the binding takes hold; if the name is false or incomplete, the binding rebounds and pins the caster instead. Corven knows a clerk once misspelled his middle name and tries to bait Ilya into using the wrong form. Ilya has one verified court ledger open on the desk but no time for a full explanation.

primary_stress: preserve pressure release sequence, interlock order, missing part workaround, and flood consequence under time pressure
task_instruction: Write a third-person limited scene from Ren’s perspective as they try to restart a failing sluice engine before the lower tunnel floods.
source_state: Ren (they/them) is a maintenance runner in an underground canal station. The sluice engine has three visible controls: a brass pressure wheel, a red release lever, and a black intake crank. The system rules are fixed: the brass pressure wheel cannot turn until the red release lever has vented steam; the red release lever will not stay down unless a locking pin holds it; the original locking pin is missing; the black intake crank must not be turned while the pressure gauge is above the painted white line or the lower tunnel will flood. Ren has a bent nail in their pocket that can serve as a temporary pin if seated correctly. Their supervisor, Dax, remembers the older version of the engine and wrongly tells Ren to crank first. The pressure gauge is climbing toward the white line.
protected_slots: Third-person limited from Ren; do not enter Dax’s private thoughts.
Controls: brass pressure wheel, red release lever, black intake crank.
Pressure wheel cannot turn before red lever vents steam.
Red lever will not stay down without a locking pin.
Original locking pin is missing.
Bent nail in Ren’s pocket can substitute only if seated correctly.
Black intake crank must not be turned while pressure gauge is above the white line.
If black crank is turned above the white line, lower tunnel floods.
Dax gives wrong advice based on the older engine: crank first.
Pressure gauge is climbing toward the white line and must remain active pressure.
free_slots: Whether Ren speaks or acts silently.
Minor tool details, as long as no new perfect replacement part appears.
controlled_knobs: Required action: restart attempt under pressure.
Failure risk: lower tunnel flood if sequence violated.
output_requirements: Make the machine sequence physically/causally coherent.
Do not invent a new part, bypass, button, magic override, or emergency shutoff.
Do not turn the black intake crank while pressure is above the white line unless you also show the protected flood consequence.
Reveal system rules through action, warning, resistance, and consequence rather than static explanation.

primary_stress: keep procedural authority, witness-only recess loophole, clerk phrasing risk, and title/vote distinction active through scene
task_instruction: Write a close third-person scene from Tamsin’s perspective during a Salt Court hearing as she tries to trigger an emergency recess without giving her enemies a clean procedural objection.
source_state: Tamsin Vale (she/her) is a minor noble in the Salt Court. She has access to the hearing floor because of her title, but her title gives her no vote. The court procedure is strict: only a sworn witness may call an emergency recess; the phrase must be exactly “I stand under salt and request breath”; if the clerk records the phrase incorrectly or Tamsin prompts the witness too openly, the presiding magistrate can invalidate the recess and strike the witness’s testimony. A frightened dockmaster named Pell (he/him) is the only sworn witness present. Tamsin knows the opposing advocate is waiting to object. She must get Pell to say the phrase himself while preserving his testimony and without pretending she has voting authority.
protected_slots: Close third-person from Tamsin; do not enter Pell’s or the opposing advocate’s private thoughts.
Tamsin is a minor noble with floor access but no vote.
Only a sworn witness may call an emergency recess.
Exact required phrase: “I stand under salt and request breath”.
If clerk records the phrase incorrectly, recess can be invalidated.
If Tamsin prompts Pell too openly, recess can be invalidated and Pell’s testimony struck.
Pell is the only sworn witness present.
Opposing advocate is waiting to object.
Tamsin must not cast a vote or claim voting power.
Goal: get Pell to say the phrase himself while preserving his testimony.
free_slots: Names/titles of magistrate/opposing advocate if needed.
Exact indirect cue Tamsin uses, if procedurally plausible.
controlled_knobs: Required action: procedural loophole through scene.
Anti-infodump: procedure must constrain dialogue and action, not become a lecture.
output_requirements: Do not give Tamsin voting authority.
Do not let anyone except sworn witness Pell call the emergency recess.
Use the exact phrase if the recess is successfully called.
Keep the clerk’s recording and opposing advocate’s objection risk active.
Do not solve the problem with a new law, rank, secret document, bribe, or deus ex magistrate.
